mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for S&P 500 constituents and results in negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive momentum in housing starts (HOUST) above a 6-month moving average, combined with rising personal savings (RSAFS), signals improved household balance sheets and higher future consumption, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 3-month moving average by more than 1% month-over-month indicates robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS jumps above its 3-month moving average by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals reduced household precautionary balances, which increases reliance on credit and may constrain consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of the economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.
